title: Cajun Chicken Pasta (Creamy Rigatoni Meal Prep)
description: One-skillet Cajun chicken with peppers, onion, and rigatoni simmered in broth, finished with cream cheese + Parmesan into a thick orange creamy sauce. Six meal-prep bowls.
steps: Flatten breasts, cube bite-size. Season with salt, onion powder, garlic powder, paprika, Italian seasoning, Cajun. Mix by hand.
Oil a hot skillet. Sear chicken until browned, ~5–6 min.
Add diced peppers and onion; stir. Add minced garlic; stir.
Add dry rigatoni. Pour in broth + ~1 cup water until pasta is just covered. Pinch of salt. Bring to boil.
Cover, simmer 12–15 min, stirring once, until pasta is tender and most liquid is absorbed.
Lower heat. Stir in cream cheese block + shredded cheese until melted into a thick orange creamy sauce.
Scoop into 6 bowls. Fridge 4–5 days; reheat with a splash of water or broth.
notes: One-pan meal prep. Pasta should be just covered — not swimming. Cream cheese melts into the residual broth; stir until glossy and coated.

title: Street Corn Bowl | 55g Protein
description: Charred taco-spiced chicken over white rice with creamy Cotija elote salad and Tajín. Five kraft-bowl meal preps — 55g protein each.

items.name: kosher salt, chili powder, Tajín (1–2 tbsp)
cooked white rice (~3/4 cup per bowl)

steps: Flatten chicken slightly for even cooking. Coat in chili powder, smoked paprika, cumin, garlic, onion powder, salt, pepper.
Cook in a hot skillet/electric pan with oil spray, lid on medium-high, ~6–7 min per side until charred and 165°F. Rest, cube.
Elote: mix corn, Greek yogurt, mayo, Cotija, red onion. Fold in jalapeño, cilantro, lime. Season with salt, chili powder, 1–2 tbsp Tajín until creamy.
Assemble 5 bowls: rice → chicken → big scoop of street corn → more Tajín on top.
Fridge 4–5 days.
notes: Same elote vibe as the pasta salad / sweet potato bowls, but rice base. Flatten chicken for even sear. 55g protein per bowl as labeled in the reel.

title: 51g Protein Elote Chicken Pasta Salad
description: Smoky taco-seasoned chicken, charred corn, tri-color rotini, Cotija, and creamy Tajín Greek yogurt sauce. Cold pasta salad energy — 51g protein per bowl, 5 meal-prep containers.

items.name: chili powder, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, salt + pepper

steps: Season chicken heavily both sides. Sear on a hot griddle/flat-top with oil spray until charred and 165°F inside. Rest, then dice.
Boil rotini in salted water until al dente. Drain.
Char corn: hot dry pan, no liquid. Sit 4–5 min until golden; stir once.
Huge bowl: rotini, diced chicken, charred corn, cilantro, red onion, Cotija. Lime juice, Greek yogurt, mayo, spice mix + Tajín. Mix until creamy and coated. More Tajín on top.
Divide into 5 containers. Fridge 4–5 days. Serve cold / room temp.
notes: Char on chicken + corn is the flavor. Don't skip Tajín. Meal-prep king — 5 bowls like the reel.

title: Loaded Sweet Potato with Elote + Taco Beef
description: Baked sweet potato half stuffed with seasoned lean taco beef and creamy Mexican street corn salad. 47g protein per bowl — meal-prep tray friendly.

items.name: sweet corn kernels (thawed frozen or drained canned)
Tajín, chili powder, garlic powder, salt + pepper

steps: Roast: halve sweet potatoes lengthwise. Oil, salt, pepper. Cut-side down on a sheet pan. Bake 425°F / 220°C for 35–45 min until soft and caramelized.
Elote: mix corn, Greek yogurt, mayo, most of the Cotija, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro, lime juice. Season with Tajín, chili powder, garlic powder, salt, pepper. Taste — creamy, salty, limey, spicy.
Beef: oil a pan, brown lean ground beef with cumin/garlic/onion (or taco seasoning), salt, pepper. Cook until no pink. Drain if needed.
Assemble: smash one sweet potato half open in a bowl. ~4 oz beef, big scoop of corn salad. Finish with Cotija, Tajín, cilantro, lime wedge.
notes: Makes 4 bowls on one tray — meal-prep friendly. Leaner beef = higher protein. Elote should taste aggressively limey/Tajín before it hits the potato.

title: Şifa Çorbası (Creamy Chicken & Vegetable Soup)
description: Turkish healing soup — chicken breast layered over veg, simmered, shredded, then the pot blended silky with no cream or flour. Finish with turmeric, paprika, parsley, and lemon. ~280–320 cal / ~28g protein per bowl.

items.name: potatoes, peeled and cubed (Yukon Gold if possible)
hot water to cover (or bone broth)

steps: Layer in a large pot: potatoes, carrots, red pepper, onion, garlic, and tomatoes. Lay whole chicken breasts on top.
Drizzle olive oil, pour hot water to just cover. Lid on — simmer until chicken and potatoes are fully tender, ~25–30 min.
Pull chicken out with tongs; shred in a bowl with two forks.
Blend remaining vegetables + broth in the pot (immersion blender) until smooth and bright orange-creamy.
Return shredded chicken. Season with salt, turmeric, paprika, black pepper, and a big handful of parsley. Stir 2–3 min.
Ladle into bowls and squeeze fresh lemon on top — that's key.
notes: Creaminess is 100% from blended potato/carrot/tomato — no cream, no flour. Air-chilled chicken stays juicier. Kapya → red bell is fine. Hot water works; bone broth upgrades depth. Gluten-free, dairy-free, recovery-friendly.

title: THE Ultimate Pepper Chicken (Ghee Roast Style)
description: Restaurant-style pepper chicken — yogurt-marinated thighs, golden onions, dum-cooked (no stirring), finished with fresh roasted fennel-pepper powder and curry leaves. ~300 cal / 40g protein per serving.
steps: Marinate: mix chicken with chili, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, salt, and yogurt. Rest 20–30 min.
Golden onions: heat sesame oil in a wide pan. Sauté sliced onions on medium until deep golden brown — don't rush.
Dum cook: add all marinated chicken on top of the onions, spread out. DO NOT STIR. Cover and cook medium-low 15 min so the chicken releases its own water.
Fresh masala: meanwhile toast fennel + peppercorns dry 2–3 min until aromatic. Cool slightly, grind coarse (not super fine).
Finish: uncover, add fennel-pepper powder + curry leaves. Mix. Cook uncovered 7–8 min until dark, dry, glossy, and roasty — not gravy. Adjust salt/pepper.
Serve: banana leaf energy — with hot ghee rice, chapati, parotta, roti, or as a wrap.
notes: Thighs not breast. No water. No stirring for the first 15 min = caramelized onion + chicken flavor. Fresh pepper powder beats store-bought. Splash more sesame oil at the end for restaurant gloss.

title: Halal Cart Chicken and Rice
description: NYC cart energy at home — charred spiced thighs, turmeric rice, and that iconic white sauce.

items.name: white sauce, red hot sauce, parsley

steps: Marinate chicken with oil, vinegar, lemon & spices 20 min, then sear until charred and cooked through.
Toast rice with oil, butter, turmeric & spices, add stock, simmer covered 15 min until fluffy.
Whisk mayo, sour cream, lemon, garlic, salt & pepper; chill to thicken.
Pile rice, top with chicken, drizzle both sauces, scatter parsley.
notes: Char on the chicken is the whole point — don't crowd the pan.

title: High-Protein Tomato Basil Soup
description: Shred Happens style — roasted veg blended with bone broth and cottage cheese. ~79g protein total.
steps: Sheet pan tomatoes, onion, pepper, garlic with oil + spices.
Roast at 400°F for 60 min till caramelized and tender.
Blend roasted veg with bone broth + cottage cheese + basil till smooth and creamy.
Bowl it up — oil/cream drizzle, fresh basil, parmesan optional.
notes: Roast until deeply caramelized — pale veg = flat soup.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
description: Real Roman carbonara — no cream. Guanciale, tempered eggs, Pecorino silk.
steps: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a rolling boil.
Cut guanciale into lardons. Render in a cold pan over medium-low ~8 min until crispy at edges. Keep warm off heat.
Whisk eggs, yolks, and most of the cheese. Season hard with black pepper.
Cook spaghetti until 90 seconds shy of al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water.
Toss drained pasta in guanciale fat off heat.
Pour egg mixture over pasta, tossing constantly. Splash pasta water until glossy. Don't scramble.
Plate warm. Finish with cheese and pepper.
notes: Off-heat is non-negotiable. Residual heat finishes the eggs.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Char-edged tikka in a silky tomato-cream masala built on toasted spices.
ingredients: Marinade: 180g yogurt, 2 tsp garam masala, 1½ tsp cumin, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri chili, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp oil
3 tbsp ghee, 1 large onion finely diced
2 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp coriander seeds (toasted, ground)
1 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp garam masala, 1½ tsp Kashmiri chili
steps: Marinate chicken min 4 hours (overnight best).
Broil/grill until deeply charred, 8–10 min per side.
Ghee + cumin seeds 30 sec. Onion 12–15 min until deep gold.
Garlic + ginger 2 min. Ground spices 1 min.
Tomatoes 15 min uncovered until oil separates.
Add chicken + cream. Simmer 8 min. Cilantro finish.
notes: Char is flavor — don't skip the broil.

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in spiced tomato-pepper sauce. One pan, celebratory Tuesday energy.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, ½ tsp caraway, pinch cayenne
steps: Onion + pepper in oil, 8 min until soft.
Garlic + spices 1–2 min.
Tomatoes + sugar, simmer 10 min until thick.
Make wells, crack eggs in.
Cover 5–8 min until whites just set, yolks runny.
Feta, parsley, olive oil. Serve from the pan.
notes: Pull when whites look barely set — residual heat finishes them.
